universalAnswers.whatHappened: OpenAI called on Congress September 9 to enact mandatory capability-based safety rules for the most capable AI labs; Sanders and Casar had announced a separate, forthcoming pause-and-ban proposal September 3.
universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: These are proposals for how government could control the most capable AI development, not new product features or current legal duties.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: OpenAI’s complete policy statement, the Sanders office’s complete announcement and Reuters reporting were independently reopened September 11.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: OpenAI is advocating its preferred framework. The lawmakers describe their legislation as forthcoming. The sources do not establish formal bill text, passage, effectiveness or a new federal law.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: The rules would decide which developers must test, disclose, slow or stop before the most capable systems move forward; readers need to know whether a policy headline changes rights or obligations today.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: The proposals directly target frontier AI developers and federal oversight, with wider public consequences claimed but not yet demonstrated.
universalAnswers.changesNow: The public record now contains a major AI company’s call for binding federal requirements and a lawmakers’ announced alternative; legal obligations remain unchanged by these announcements.
universalAnswers.uncertainty: Formal legislative text, definitions, enforcement details, political support, passage and real-world effectiveness remain unresolved.
universalAnswers.readerAction: Classify the source as company position, announced proposal, introduced bill or enacted law, then identify the covered systems and trigger.
universalAnswers.betterQuestion: Who is proposing the rule, what legal vehicle exists, which systems would it cover and what event would trigger testing, reporting, slowing or stopping?

legal-policy.legalStatus: OpenAI’s September 9 post is a company request. The Sanders-Casar September 3 source calls its legislation forthcoming. Neither source establishes enacted federal law.
legal-policy.jurisdiction: Both proposals concern United States federal policy for advanced AI development; OpenAI also calls for compatible international standards.
legal-policy.parties: OpenAI asks Congress for targeted requirements; Senator Bernie Sanders and Representative Greg Casar announced a broader pause-and-ban proposal; Congress would have to act for either to become federal law.
legal-policy.allegationVsFinding: Risk and benefit claims remain the speakers’ arguments. The verified event is the publication of the proposals and their stated scope.
legal-policy.currentEffect: No federal safety duty is created by either announcement. OpenAI says voluntary standards would complement rather than replace mandatory safeguards.
legal-policy.unresolvedQuestions: Formal bill text, exact definitions, enforcement, legislative support, passage and effectiveness remain open.
legal-policy.nextMilestone: A formal bill number or text, committee action, enacted legislation or a materially revised company position would change the status.

company-business.businessChange: OpenAI publicly shifted toward asking Congress for mandatory national requirements aimed at the handful of best-resourced frontier labs.
company-business.companyMotive: The article does not claim a motive; the company presents safety, public trust, competition and U.S. leadership as reasons.
company-business.payer: The sources do not quantify compliance costs or who ultimately bears them.
company-business.beneficiary: OpenAI says the framework would reduce public risk and concentration of power; those are expected benefits, not measured outcomes.
company-business.incentives: Capability thresholds would make obligations rise with demonstrated power and risk, while OpenAI says smaller developers should remain outside frontier duties.
company-business.customerEffectNow: No current user setting, product right or purchase changes because of the policy post.
company-business.financialContext: The sources provide no reviewed cost estimate or market-impact evidence.

translation.newsVersionExact: OpenAI asked Congress on September 9 to create mandatory national safety rules for the most capable AI systems.
translation.actualMeaningExact: Its preferred framework includes common testing, independent assessments, cybersecurity protections and clear reporting of serious incidents.
translation.mechanismExact: OpenAI’s is capability-based: rules become stronger as a system’s demonstrated abilities and risks increase.
